info.title: Publishing API
info.description: Social accounts, posts, scheduling, approval, tags, media and analytics for one workspace. Authenticate with a workspace API key or a personal access token; the workspace UUID is part of every URL.

domain.description: The domain you sign in to, without https://

tags.name: Analytics
tags.description: Followers, reach, engagement and post performance, as the analytics dashboard shows them, plus when to post. Dates are UTC days unless a `timezone` is sent. Figures compared with the previous period of the same length are `{value, change}`, where `change` is a percentage (`100` when the previous period was zero, `null` when both are). Time series are lists of `{date, value}` points; breakdowns (ages, countries, keywords) are lists of `{label, value}`.

bearerAuth.description: A workspace API key (`Authorization: Bearer osk_...`) or a personal access token.

apiKeyHeader.name: x-api-key
apiKeyHeader.description: A workspace API key in the `x-api-key` header. Personal access tokens must use `Authorization: Bearer`.

profile_url.description: The account's profile on the network.

external_url.description: Link to this account's copy of the post on the network, once published. Only in a post's `accounts`.

errors.description: Why publishing failed on this account. Only in a post's `accounts`.

published_parts.description: How many of this account's items are live: the post, then its first comment or thread replies. A failed account can have some. Only in a post's `accounts`.

id.description: Use this in a post version's `media`.

is_processing.description: `true` while the file is still being processed.

duration_ms.description: Video length in milliseconds. `null` for images, and for a video not read yet.

folder.description: The folder the item is filed in, or `null` at the top level.

status.description: `publishing` while the post is going out.

publish_progress.description: Only while the post is publishing: how many of its accounts are done.

account_id.description: `0` for the original version. Otherwise an account `id` that is also in `accounts`, to override the content for that account.

is_original.description: Only the first version is the original.

synced_with.description: The `account_id` of the version this one copies its content from (`0` for the original), or `null`.

content.description: Most posts have a single item. A second item is posted as the first comment on Facebook Pages, Instagram, LinkedIn and YouTube, and as a reply that starts a thread on X, Bluesky, Mastodon, Threads and Pixelfed, where each further item continues the thread. Other networks publish only the first item. A first comment needs text; on Facebook Pages and LinkedIn it can also carry one image or GIF, and on Instagram and YouTube it takes no media.

body.description: Multi-line text comes back as HTML, one `<div>` per line.

media.description: Media objects. In requests you send media `id`s instead.

options.description: Network-specific options, keyed by provider (for example a Reddit title).

message.example: The date range may span at most 366 days.

date_to: The date range may span at most 366 days.

AnalyticsPeriod.description: The range the figures cover, and the previous range of the same length every `change` is measured against.

change.description: Percent against the previous period: `100` when that was zero and this is not, `null` when both are zero.

date.description: A UTC day, or a month (`YYYY-MM`).

growth_rate.description: Percent of the followers at the start.

best_account.description: Highest growth rate; null with no accounts.

needs_attention.description: Lowest growth rate, only when negative; otherwise null.

audience_chart.description: Total followers per day; `null` where nothing was recorded.

least_active.description: Fewest posts; null when it is the most active account.

progress.description: Percent while the first import runs.

data.description: Depends on the network and type. Compared figures are `{value, change}`, time series `{date, value}` lists, breakdowns `{label, value}` lists, and charts with several series an object of such lists.

has_data.description: False, with neutral scores and no `best`, when no account has scored history.

day_intervals.description: Seven lists, Sunday first, of twelve two-hour intervals. `end_hour` is exclusive.

summary.description: Empty when the post went out to no account yet.

engagement_rate.description: Likes, comments and shares as a percent of views.

breakdown.description: Empty when there was no engagement.

winner.description: The account with the highest engagement rate; null with fewer than two accounts or no engagement.

breakdown.description: Empty when there was no engagement.

vs_average.description: Against that account's average post: `1.3` is 30% above. Null without an average.

PostRequirementsFailed.description: The post breaks a rule of one of its networks, so nothing was saved or scheduled. Each key is `requirements.{version}.{provider}.{rule}`. `{version}` is the `account_id` of the version at fault (`0` for the original), or the account `id` when the rule is about that account's own option, such as a Pinterest board. A rule about content ends in the content item's position, from `0`. Examples: `requirements.0.instagram.hashtags_0` (more than 5 hashtags), `requirements.0.instagram.post_0` (an Instagram feed post with no media), `requirements.12.pinterest.board` (no board), `requirements.0.twitter.text_0` (over 280 characters on an account without X Premium), `requirements.0.facebook_page.first_comment` (a second item with no text on a network that posts it as the first comment) and `requirements.0.instagram.first_comment_media` (media in an Instagram first comment). The same request's other checks can add other keys, such as `cannot_scheduled`.

post.description:
Creates a draft, or schedules it if you set `schedule`, `schedule_now` or `queue` (which also needs at least one account). `schedule` needs `date` and `time`; without them the post is saved as a draft. `queue` gives each account its own next free slot in its posting schedule, and the post's `scheduled_at` is the earliest of them. Each line of `body` becomes a paragraph.

When you schedule, queue or publish now, the post is first checked against each network's rules, such as Instagram's limit of 5 hashtags or Pinterest's board. If it breaks one you get `422` and nothing is created. Drafts are not checked.

**Required permission:** `publishing:posts:write`, plus `publishing:posts:publish` to schedule, queue or publish now.

put.description:
Replaces the post's accounts, tags, date, time and versions. `date` and `time` are read in `timezone`, or without it in the timezone setting of the key's creator (or the token's user), then UTC. To schedule, call [Schedule a post](/publishing/posts/schedule-a-post) afterwards. A non-draft post with no accounts or no date and time goes back to draft.

A scheduled post that stays scheduled is first checked against each network's rules. If it breaks one you get `422` and nothing changes.

**Required permission:** `publishing:posts:write`, plus `publishing:posts:publish` if the post is scheduled or you send a `date` and `time`.

post.description:
Schedules the post, or publishes it now with `postNow: true`. Send `date` and `time` to set its time here; without them it keeps its saved date and time. `postNow` sends every account now and drops their own times. The post may need approval first.

The post is first checked against each network's rules, such as Instagram's limit of 5 hashtags or Pinterest's board. If it breaks one you get `422` and nothing is scheduled.

**Required permission:** `publishing:posts:publish`

Puts the post in the queue. Each account gets its own next free slot in its posting schedule, and the post's `scheduled_at` is the earliest of them. The slots follow each posting schedule's own timezone.

The post is first checked against each network's rules, such as Instagram's limit of 5 hashtags or Pinterest's board. If it breaks one you get `422` and nothing is scheduled.

post.description:
Approves a post that is waiting for approval, and schedules it. Send `date` and `time` (or `accounts_schedule`) to change its time as you approve; without them it keeps the time it was submitted with. The key's creator (or the token's user) must be allowed to approve posts.

The post is first checked against each network's rules, such as Instagram's limit of 5 hashtags or Pinterest's board. If it breaks one you get `422` and the post keeps waiting for approval.

**Required permission:** `publishing:posts:approve`

get.description:
Every account in the workspace that has analytics, over one period: total followers, follower growth and posts with their change, the best-growing account and one losing followers, a leaderboard, the most and least active accounts, each account's share of followers, total followers per day, and on how many days anything was posted.

Read-only. Personal access tokens may call it with any workspace role, viewers included. If your platform has turned analytics off, every analytics endpoint answers `404`.

**Required permission:** `publishing:analytics:read`

parameters.name: workspace
parameters.description: Your workspace UUID. With a workspace API key it must be the key's workspace; a personal access token works in every workspace you belong to.

parameters.name: period
parameters.description: In UTC. Weeks start on Monday. `this_week`, `this_month` and `this_year` run up to today; `last_3_months` is the three whole months before this one. Ignored when `date_from` and `date_to` are both sent.

parameters.name: date_from
parameters.description: Start of a custom range (UTC day). Send with `date_to`.

parameters.name: date_to
parameters.description: End of a custom range, on or after `date_from`. A range spans at most 366 days, both ends included.

403.description: The API key does not have `publishing:analytics:read`.

404.description: Unknown workspace, account or post, or analytics are turned off.

422.description: Invalid input. An unknown `period`, one date without the other, an end before the start, or more than 366 days.

get.summary: Get the analytics of an account
get.description:
One account's analytics of one `type`. The answer's `tabs` lists the types the account supports, which depend on the network:

| Network | Types |
| --- | --- |
| Instagram | overview, engagement, audience, reach, content, hashtags, insights, competitors (competitors needs an account connected through Facebook) |
| Facebook Page | overview, engagement, video, content, hashtags, insights |
| Google Business Profile | overview, engagement, content, search_terms, reviews |
| Threads, Bluesky, Mastodon, LinkedIn Page | overview, engagement, content, hashtags, insights |
| Pinterest | overview, content, hashtags, insights |
| TikTok, YouTube | overview, content, insights |
| LinkedIn profile | overview, engagement |

Accounts on other networks (X among them) have no analytics and get a `422`. `data` depends on the network and type. `content` lists the period's posts with their metrics, paged (`data.pagination`) and sortable by a metric; `reviews` pages too. `insights` gives the best day, hour, post type and posting frequency, the top post and the engagement trend. While `initial_sync.in_progress` is true, the account's first import is still running and the figures are incomplete.

Read-only. Personal access tokens may call it with any workspace role, viewers included. If your platform has turned analytics off, every analytics endpoint answers `404`.

**Required permission:** `publishing:analytics:read`

get.summary: Get the best times to post
get.description:
When posting has worked, per weekday and hour, pooled over the chosen accounts. Each post of the last 180 days that has views counts by its engagement rate against its own account's average, and every account weighs the same, so a busy account does not drown out the others. A slot scores 50 × that ratio, pulled toward 50 when few posts are behind it, from 0 to 100: 50 is average for these accounts, 100 twice the average or better. Only networks with the `insights` type take part.

Weekdays run from `0` (Sunday) to `6` (Saturday). `best` names up to three slots with at least two posts behind them, at most one per weekday, highest first. `confidence` is `high` from 5 posts, `medium` from 2, `low` with 1 and `none` without. `offset_hours` is the timezone's offset from UTC now.

Read-only. Personal access tokens may call it with any workspace role, viewers included. If your platform has turned analytics off, every analytics endpoint answers `404`.

**Required permission:** `publishing:analytics:read`

parameters.name: workspace
parameters.description: Your workspace UUID. With a workspace API key it must be the key's workspace; a personal access token works in every workspace you belong to.

parameters.name: accounts[]
parameters.description: Account UUIDs. Defaults to every account in the workspace.

parameters.name: timezone
parameters.description: IANA timezone the weekdays, hours and times are in. Defaults to the timezone setting of the key's creator (or the token's user), then UTC.

404.description: Unknown workspace, account or post, or analytics are turned off.

422.description: Invalid input. An account that is not in the workspace (`accounts.0`), or an unknown timezone.

get.summary: Get the next best time for each account
get.description:
Each account is scored on its own history, as in *Get the best times to post*, and its next best time is the soonest of its `best` slots after `from`. That is always within a week, and never in the past. Accounts with no best slot yet are left out of `times`.

Read-only. Personal access tokens may call it with any workspace role, viewers included. If your platform has turned analytics off, every analytics endpoint answers `404`.

**Required permission:** `publishing:analytics:read`

get.summary: Get the analytics of a post
get.description:
How a post did on each account it went out to. Accounts it did not go out to are left out, so a post that is not published yet has an empty `summary` and `accounts`. Trashed posts can still be read. Trends are daily; a post tracked for 60 days or more is grouped by week (each point dated with its Monday), and one tracked for 180 days or more by month (`YYYY-MM`).

Read-only. Personal access tokens may call it with any workspace role, viewers included. If your platform has turned analytics off, every analytics endpoint answers `404`.

**Required permission:** `publishing:analytics:read`

parameters.name: workspace
parameters.description: Your workspace UUID. With a workspace API key it must be the key's workspace; a personal access token works in every workspace you belong to.

parameters.name: post
parameters.description: Post UUID.
